open_points.subject: owner-session expiry pass
open_points.text: “at a pass over the sessions it makes every 60 seconds from the start”
open_points.question: Does the first expiry pass run at instance start or 60 seconds later, and are later passes fixed to the start-time cadence or scheduled 60 seconds after the previous pass finishes?
options: First at start, then fixed 60-second boundaries
First after 60 seconds, then fixed boundaries
Sixty seconds after each completed pass
open_points.default_guess: Run the first pass 60 seconds after start and use fixed 60-second boundaries.

open_points.subject: owner-session lifetime
open_points.text: “8 hours after sign-in; 30 minutes without an owner request”
open_points.question: Are these durations measured with the UTC wall clock or a monotonic elapsed-time clock, and what happens when the system clock moves backward or forward?
options: Use monotonic elapsed time
Use UTC wall-clock instants
Use monotonic time for idle expiry and UTC for the absolute limit
open_points.default_guess: Use monotonic elapsed time for both limits while the process lives.

open_points.subject: owner-session expiry race
open_points.text: “Validity is checked when a request arrives”; “a request that passes it completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs”; “the pass alone ends sessions by their limits, taking the import lock and then each session's lock”
open_points.question: How is admission made atomic with the expiry pass, given that a request may pass the session check before taking the session lock and the pass may then remove the session, confirmation, or uploaded file before that admitted request uses them?
options: Take or reserve the session under its lock during the session check
Track admitted in-flight requests and defer removal until they finish
Allow removal and require the admitted request to continue from captured state
open_points.default_guess: Perform the validity check and last-request update under the session lock, and defer absolute-expiry removal while an admitted request is in flight.

open_points.subject: owner-session expiry pass traversal
open_points.text: “a pass over the sessions … taking the import lock and then each session's lock … and deciding under them”
open_points.question: Which sessions belong to a pass, is the import lock held for the whole pass or reacquired for each session, and is expiry tested against one pass-start instant or the instant each session lock is acquired?
options: Snapshot sessions and time at pass start; hold one import lock throughout
Snapshot sessions at pass start; test time per session; hold one import lock throughout
Re-enumerate and reacquire the import lock per session
open_points.default_guess: Snapshot the session identities at pass start, hold the import lock throughout, and test expiry when each session lock is acquired.

open_points.subject: accepted import and other sessions
open_points.text: “every other request that reads or changes an uploaded file … take the instance's one import lock first, then their session's lock”; “an accepted import, holding it, drops every session's upload”; “The requests of one owner session that change its state … are applied one at a time … [with] the session's one lock”
open_points.question: Must an accepted import take every affected session's lock before dropping that session's upload, or is the import lock alone authoritative for uploaded-file state despite the session-lock rule?
options: Import lock alone protects every uploaded file
Take all affected session locks after the import lock
Treat cross-session clearing as an explicit exception to session-state serialization
open_points.default_guess: Make the import lock the sole authority for uploaded-file state and state that cross-session clearing is an exception to the session-lock rule.

open_points.subject: accepted import upload clearing
open_points.text: “A refused confirmation keeps it”; “an accepted import … drops every session's upload”; “The import has succeeded when that transaction is committed”
open_points.question: At what point relative to the durable import transaction are all in-memory uploads dropped, and must they remain intact if the transaction fails?
options: Drop uploads only after the transaction commits
Drop them before commit and restore them on rollback
Include a reversible pending-clear step around the transaction
open_points.default_guess: Commit the transaction first, then drop all uploads while still holding the import lock and before answering.

open_points.subject: closed import upload refusal
open_points.text: “check the closure while holding them”; “when the closure exists, uploading … [is] refused”; A04 orders “the values given” before lifecycle and conflict checks
open_points.question: When the import is already closed and an upload is also oversized, unreadable, or malformed, which refusal wins, and may Registry parse or read the file before checking closure?
options: Closure is checked first and hides file errors
File/value checks follow A04 and precede closure
Both failures are returned because they occupy one stage
open_points.default_guess: Check closure immediately after authentication and locking, before reading or validating the uploaded file.

open_points.subject: configuration variables
open_points.text: “The configuration is the set of environment variables whose names begin with REGISTRY_ … It holds exactly these items”
open_points.question: What is the exact environment-variable name for each listed item, including each of the four service tokens?
options: One fixed name per item declared here
Names declared later by the release
A structured convention derived from service names
open_points.default_guess: Use fixed uppercase names such as REGISTRY_STORE_LOCATION, REGISTRY_BACKUP_LOCATION, REGISTRY_BACKUP_KEY, REGISTRY_OWNER_CREDENTIAL, and REGISTRY_TOKEN_<SERVICE>.

open_points.subject: configuration values and secrets
open_points.text: “each well formed”; “A secret … is at least 32 bytes long”
open_points.question: What encodings and grammars make paths, tokens, the owner credential, and the backup key well formed, and are the 32 bytes counted before or after decoding an environment-variable string?
options: UTF-8 text secrets, length measured after UTF-8 encoding
Base64-encoded random bytes, length measured after decoding
Different declared formats for credentials, tokens, and encryption keys
open_points.default_guess: Require base64-encoded bytes for all secrets, measure decoded length, and require exactly 32 decoded bytes for the backup key.

open_points.subject: configuration paths
open_points.text: “compared by their absolute paths with every symbolic link resolved”
open_points.question: Are relative store or backup paths accepted, and if so, against which stable directory are they made absolute?
options: Reject every relative path
Resolve relative paths against the process working directory
Resolve them against a release-defined data directory
open_points.default_guess: Reject relative paths and require absolute configured paths.

open_points.subject: new-store temporary file
open_points.text: “under a temporary name — the store's name with a suffix the release declares”
open_points.question: What suffix does the release declare, how is collision with an existing non-temporary file prevented, and where is that declaration recorded for later implementations?
options: A fixed specification-wide suffix
A release-manifest field
A newly random temporary suffix on each start
open_points.default_guess: Use one fixed suffix declared in the release manifest and refuse unsafe collisions.

open_points.subject: backup encryption
open_points.text: “Each backup is encrypted with the backup key”; “A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with”
open_points.question: Which authenticated-encryption algorithm, nonce generation rule, key size and encoding, file framing, associated data, and authentication-failure behavior define an encrypted backup?
options: AES-256-GCM with a random nonce and authenticated metadata
XChaCha20-Poly1305 with a random nonce and authenticated metadata
A standard encrypted-container format fixed by the release
open_points.default_guess: Use XChaCha20-Poly1305 with a 32-byte decoded key, a fresh random nonce, and authenticate all unencrypted metadata as associated data.

open_points.subject: backup key digest
open_points.text: “a digest of the key it was made with (never the key)”
open_points.question: Which digest algorithm and byte representation are used, and is the recorded digest verified against the configured key during the make-and-check run?
options: SHA-256 of the decoded key, verified during the run
A keyed identifier derived with HKDF
An opaque key identifier supplied in configuration
open_points.default_guess: Record SHA-256 of the decoded backup key and verify it during the backup check.

open_points.subject: backup file format and names
open_points.text: “Kept and temporary names begin with two different prefixes the release declares”; “A kept name is made from the backup's instant”; “its unencrypted record … can be read”
open_points.question: What are the two prefixes, the kept-name timestamp representation and precision, and the exact serialized layout and versioning of the unencrypted record and encrypted payload?
options: A specification-wide versioned binary container and fixed filename grammar
A release-manifest declaration of prefixes and container version
Implementation-private names and serialization
open_points.default_guess: Define a versioned binary container and fixed ASCII filenames containing a UTC timestamp with subsecond precision and a random collision-resistant suffix.

open_points.subject: backup record validity
open_points.text: “a kept file's record is valid when its instant, release, last sequence number and key digest can all be read”
open_points.question: Does ‘can all be read’ require only syntactic decoding, or also valid ranges, a known release, a non-future instant, a correctly sized digest, and consistency between the record and ciphertext?
options: Syntactic decoding only
Full semantic and cryptographic consistency validation
Semantic validation except that old or unknown releases remain valid
open_points.default_guess: Require full syntactic, range, and cryptographic consistency validation, while allowing a recorded older release identifier.

open_points.subject: backup audit sequence
open_points.text: “records … the last audit sequence number it holds”; “checks … that its audit log ends at the recorded sequence number”
open_points.question: Is the recorded number the persistent highest-ever sequence counter or the greatest surviving AuditEntry sequence, and what value represents a new store with no audit entries?
options: Persistent highest-ever counter, with 0 for no entries
Greatest surviving entry, with null for no entries
Both values are recorded and checked separately
open_points.default_guess: Record the persistent highest-ever counter, use 0 before the first entry, and require the greatest surviving entry to equal it whenever entries exist.
